extracted.intended_audience: Voters and citizens of New York evaluating the proposed U.S. Constitution (general public interested in constitutional design)
extracted.subtask_description: Arguments and standards for how the national government should be empowered to tax and how representation should function—covering concurrent jurisdiction, uniformity, methods of collection, apportionment, and the character of representatives. Focused guidance for evaluating the proposed constitutional provisions on revenue and representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent jurisdiction in taxation
rubrics_metrics.description: A CONCURRENT JURISDICTION in the article of taxation was the only admissible substitute for an entire subordination, in respect to this branch of power, of State authority to that of the Union.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concurrent jurisdiction reconciles an indefinite constitutional power of taxation in the Federal government with an adequate and independent power in the States to provide for their own necessities; any separation of revenue objects would sacrifice the Union's interests to State power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid restricting federal taxation to particular objects
rubrics_metrics.description: If the jurisdiction of the national government in the article of revenue should be restricted to particular objects, it would naturally occasion an undue proportion of the public burdens to fall upon those objects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limiting federal revenue to specific sources (e.g., imports only) causes oppression of particular industries and unequal distribution of taxes among states and citizens; therefore the federal power should be general/indefinite rather than confined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dangers of relying solely on import duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose the federal power of taxation were to be confined to duties on imports, the government... would frequently be tempted to extend these duties to an injurious excess.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exorbitant import duties encourage smuggling (prejudicial to fair traders and revenue), can create monopolies for manufacturers, force industry into less advantageous channels, and may fall on merchants rather than consumers when markets are oversupplied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable allocation of import duties to common stock
rubrics_metrics.description: The maxim that the consumer is the payer... it is far more equitable that the duties on imports should go into a common stock, than that they should redound to the exclusive benefit of the importing States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because merchants sometimes absorb duties and because consumption patterns vary by state, import duties should feed a national common fund rather than benefit only importing states to avoid inter-state inequality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revenue interest as a guard against extreme duties (but limited)
rubrics_metrics.description: The interest of the revenue itself would be a sufficient guard against such an extreme. I readily admit that this would be the case, as long as other resources were open; but if the avenues to them were closed, HOPE, stimulated by necessity, would beget experiments...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While fiscal self-interest restrains excessive taxation when multiple revenue sources exist, closing off other avenues can lead to harmful experimentation and overreliance on a single source; therefore maintain multiple revenue options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of census/apportionment to determine federal tax proportions
rubrics_metrics.description: The proportion of these taxes is not to be left to the discretion of the national legislature, but is to be determined by the numbers of each State, as described in the second section of the first article. An actual census or enumeration of the people must furnish the rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apportion tax obligations by population enumeration to shut the door to partiality or oppression and provide an objective rule for distribution of federal tax burdens among states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniformity requirement for duties, imposts, and excises
rubrics_metrics.description: "all duties, imposts, and excises shall be UNIFORM throughout the United States."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uniformity across states is a constitutional safeguard against discriminatory revenue laws; it helps prevent partiality and unequal burdens on different states or regions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal use of state systems and officers to execute taxes
rubrics_metrics.description: The national legislature can make use of the SYSTEM OF EACH STATE WITHIN THAT STATE... the probability is that the United States will either wholly abstain from the objects preoccupied for local purposes, or will make use of the State officers and State regulations for collecting the additional imposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To avoid duplication, expense, and political friction, federal tax collection can employ existing state assessment methods and officers where practical; this is a practicable expedient to prevent double bureaucracies and alienation of state governments and people.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation of execution of land taxes to local assessors
rubrics_metrics.description: Land taxes are commonly laid... either by ACTUAL valuations... or by OCCASIONAL assessments, at the discretion... of certain officers whose duty it is to make them. In either case, the EXECUTION of the business... must be devolved upon discreet persons in the character of commissioners or assessors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While the legislature prescribes general outlines, practical execution (valuations, assessments) requires local, discreet officers (elected or appointed); national laws need not provide minute local detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding double taxation and duplication of officers
rubrics_metrics.description: As to the first point, there are two cases in which there can be no room for double sets of officers... In other cases, the probability is that the United States will either wholly abstain... or will make use of the State officers and State regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The federal government should either avoid taxing objects already regulated by states or use state collection mechanisms to prevent duplicate tax burdens and redundant administrative structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal power retained as option to strengthen requisitions
rubrics_metrics.description: If the exercise of that power [internal taxation] should be discovered on experiment to be really inconvenient, the federal government may then forbear the use of it, and have recourse to requisitions... The existence of such a power in the Constitution will have a strong influence in giving efficacy to requisitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retain internal taxation power in the Constitution as an option: its mere existence increases leverage on states to comply with requisitions and provides the federal government with a fallback if requisitions prove insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mutual forbearance to avoid policy interference
rubrics_metrics.description: An effectual expedient... will be, mutually, to abstain from those objects which either side may have first had recourse to... As neither can CONTROL the other, each will have an obvious and sensible interest in this reciprocal forbearance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where both state and federal interests exist, reciprocal abstention from overlapping revenue objects helps avoid policy clashes; practical politics will encourage such mutual accommodation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance of local knowledge delivered by representatives
rubrics_metrics.description: The knowledge of local circumstances... is it not to be presumed that the men who will generally be sent there will be possessed of the necessary degree of intelligence to be able to communicate that information?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The national legislature can obtain requisite local information through its representatives; representatives with general acquaintance of their states' resources, industries, and consumption patterns suffice for informed federal taxation decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entrust finance planning to a few enlightened statesmen/boards
rubrics_metrics.description: Nations in general... usually commit the administration of their finances to single men or to boards composed of a few individuals, who digest and prepare, in the first instance, the plans of taxation, which are afterwards passed into laws...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concentrating initial financial planning in capable ministers or boards is customary and appropriate; select inquisitive and enlightened statesmen are best qualified to design judicious revenue schemes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid concentrating taxes on particular industries or classes
rubrics_metrics.description: The confinement of the national revenues to this species of imposts would be attended with inequality... They tend to render other classes of the community tributary, in an improper degree, to the manufacturing classes...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tax policy should avoid unduly burdening particular branches of industry or classes of citizens; diversify revenue sources and be attentive to distributional effects across states, industries, and social classes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representative composition and practical representation
rubrics_metrics.description: The representative body... will consist almost entirely of proprietors of land, of merchants, and of members of the learned professions, who will truly represent all those different interests and views.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: True representation does not require literal membership from every occupation; in practice, certain broad classes (landholders, merchants, learned professions) can represent wider interests and provide necessary knowledge for governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electoral accountability creates sympathy and information
rubrics_metrics.description: Is it not natural that a man who is a candidate for the favor of the people... should take care to inform himself of their dispositions and inclinations... This dependence... are the strong chords of sympathy between the representative and the constituent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because representatives depend on voters for continuance in office and are bound by laws affecting themselves and posterity, electoral accountability incentivizes them to learn about and attend to constituents' needs and dispositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retain unpleasant powers for emergency contingencies
rubrics_metrics.description: As to poll taxes, I, without scruple, confess my disapprobation of them... But does it follow because there is a power to lay them that they will actually be laid?... The government... ought ever to have the option of making use of them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even disfavored measures (e.g., poll taxes) should remain constitutionally available as last-resort instruments for exceptional national emergencies; retaining options can be prudent despite distaste.
